title: Autoformalizing Euclidean Geometry
abstract: This paper introduces a neuro-symbolic framework for autoformalizing Euclidean geometry, combining domain knowledge, SMT solvers, and large language models. We construct LeanEuclid, a benchmark for testing machine learning on autoformalizing Euclidean geometry, and experimentally investigate the capability of GPT-4 and GPT-4V on autoformalizing theorems and proofs.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content: Imagine you're trying to understand a geometric proof, but it's written in a way that's hard to follow. That's where autoformalization comes in - it's like having a superpower that can translate informal math into formal theorems and proofs that are machine-verifiable. Euclidean geometry is a great place to start, as it provides a controllable domain for studying autoformalization. We can use Lean, a proof assistant, to write formal proofs and check their correctness.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content: Our approach uses a neuro-symbolic framework that combines domain knowledge, SMT solvers, and large language models. We use Lean to formalize Euclidean geometry problems and then use a symbolic reasoning engine to evaluate the semantics of autoformalized theorems. This engine can prove the equivalence between the ground-truth formal theorem and the autoformalized theorem, or provide partial results for fine-grained analysis.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content: We experimentally investigate the capability of GPT-4 and GPT-4V on autoformalizing theorems and proofs in Euclidean geometry. With 5-shot prompting, GPT-4 can autoformalize only 18.9% of the theorems correctly, while GPT-4V performs slightly better at 21.0%. GPT-4V can also autoformalize 23.1% of LeanEuclid proofs correctly.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content: Autoformalizing Euclidean geometry is an attractive target for AI, as it can facilitate autoformalization research to move from human inspection to automatic evaluation. This transition is essential for accelerating the development of machine learning methods on this task and ultimately easing the human effort required by formalization.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content: Our approach introduces an SMT-based symbolic engine for automatically evaluating the semantics of theorem statements in Euclidean geometry. We also demonstrate the feasibility of autoformalizing only explicit geometric proof steps, relying on the symbolic engine for implicit diagrammatic reasoning.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content: We provide the LeanEuclid benchmark, which consists of problems from Euclid's Elements and the UniGeo dataset formalized in the Lean proof assistant. You can try autoformalizing these problems using your own models and evaluate their performance using our symbolic reasoning engine.
